title: Bears safety Coby Bryant to miss 4-6 months after knee surgery
content:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. — Chicago Bears safety Coby Bryant will miss four to six months after undergoing surgery on his knee, head coach Ben Johnson announced Tuesday.

That timeline will take him out for most, if not all, of the regular season, and it’s longer than the previously reported eight to 10 weeks.

“This was what I have been told all along,” Johnson said. “We were getting opinions on it, so it’s four to six months is what I have been told.”

The Bears’ prize of free agency, Bryant signed a three-year, $40 million contract in March. In his limited time with the team, he had already impressed the Bears both on and off the field. He made an outstanding interception earlier in camp, while his teammates and coaches have raved about his work habits and leadership.

“I love his play style,” defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said last month. “I think it epitomizes the way we want to play the game.”

First-round rookie Dillon Thieneman is the other starting safety, and a major plus of having a Super Bowl-winning safety like Bryant was his ability to help Thieneman grow. Now, that challenge will fall to a different player.

Free agent acquisition Cam Lewis has gotten the first crack at replacing Bryant. The versatile defensive back moved from nickel to safety before he had to leave practice with an injury. Then it was veteran Xavier Woods, who has 121 starts in his career, including 10 last season for the Titans when he had two picks. Woods has 15 career interceptions and began his career in Dallas with Bears secondary coach Al Harris.

“He’s a veteran player. He’s played a lot of football. He’s been in a few different schemes,” Allen said of Woods on Sunday. “He’s been a productive player. … I just think right now we needed another veteran piece back there in the back end, specifically at the safety position. I’m anxious to watch him come out here and compete, you know, and see where he falls in the line.”

Elijah Hicks, who has been the Bears’ No. 3 or 4 safety since being drafted in 2022, has been on the physically-unable-to-perform list with a shin injury. He has 15 career starts.

“It certainly takes us back a little bit,” Johnson said of Bryant’s injury, “but it also provides opportunity for other guys to fill that void, and it might be guys we hope to prod along a little bit. It might be other guys who just naturally gravitate to that, but I think that’s the best thing about team sports. Normally, when there is a little bit of open air, some guys will step up to the plate and say, ‘No one else is gonna do it, so I am.’ And I think that’s gonna be a fun thing to watch.”

The pressure will ramp up on Thieneman to be ready to go from Day 1. He was drafted for his all-around skill set and his intelligence. But there’s no question the safety position takes a hit without Bryant, who could have been one of the team’s best defensive players this season.

If the Bears can make a postseason run, Bryant might be able to return. The earliest part of the four-to-six-month timeline would be mid-December, and the Bears do end their season with the Bills, Packers, Lions and Vikings. Having Bryant back in any capacity would be a major boost, but that’s a long time from now.

“Coby is the template for how we all want our team to play,” Johnson said. “He was a big part of offense, defense and special teams, the mentality, the mindset, his approach. We loved everything about him.”
